pr_title: Fix gameplay skipping forward during resume operation
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/19975.

I'm not precisely sure *where* this regressed in the changes, but it did. Rather than trying to figure out where the issue lies, I've just explicitly added this flow so we are aware of what is going on where and when.

Inline comment should explain this quite well.
pr_comments: I've took the time to debug through why this is occurring with the refactor and it turns out this is how things are supposed to work w.r.t. pause and resume: 1. `GameplayClock.Stop()` is called due to user pause, setting `IsPaused.Value = true` and transforming the frequency to zero 2. While the frequency is being adjusted, the clocks stop getting processed on `Update` 3. `GameplayClock.Start()` is called due to user resume, seeking the track to the last processed frame time, which was at the moment `Stop()` was called. This led to the realisation that `FramedBeatmapClock` actually always calls `ProcessFrame` regardless of the paused state, unlike the previous `GameplayClockContainer` version which processes the clocks only when in running state: So while the solution here is valid, the new behaviour with `FramedBeatmapClock` makes me feel slightly uneasy about it potentially regressing other scenarios, but I can't think of any in my head, so we'll see how things go.
I figured that's how things were, although for whatever reason couldn't find the code in your screenshot.

issue_context.title: Unpausing gameplay skips forwards a little bit
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

Regressed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/19828

### Screenshots or videos

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1329837/186894216-31a0257c-da24-4c97-ac6b-313059ef16bd.mp4

### Version

91e044542d5af54454282aa883727e24e6ee1baa

### Logs

-
comments: Hmm interesting. I did notice this but thought it was only jumping by the freq ramp (which has been something that historically was the case). Either way, needs to be fixed, was on my list for the clock rewrite.

review_comments: Why does this work? I've read the xmldoc and I can't understand how this being here and _not_ inside the `OnComplete()` callback below translates to the clock seeking to the correct time at unpause? Logically I would think it think it would seek to just under 200ms or so prior to the point where gameplay is fully stopped.

In `FrameStabilityClock`, as soon as it sees `IsPaused` it stops processing gameplay. So yes, you are correct in thinking that this will seek 200ms prior, but from the gameplay perspective this is where it wants to be.

I intend on addressing this in the refactor I have planned (ie. optimally no backward seek should be required. it should always go forward and everything should see that ongoing time, including `FrameStabilityClock`).
Today I learnt that gameplay is paused immediately.
Yeah, as I mentioned somewhere recently, it's not how I want it to be, but I believe it was done (temporarily) to avoid entering a `Failed` state after `Paused`. If you remember that debacle.

Perhaps renaming `StopGameplayClock` to `PauseGameplayClock` might indicate it a bit further, as I would've also thought `StopGameplayClock` to be called when the clock should just be immediately stopped.
